name: The Donnas
label: Lookout!
lede: Four Palo Alto teenagers with matching stage names, a Ramones habit and a Kiss-covering ear went from a garage to Letterman.

eras.title: Four kids, a garage, a joke band
eras.text: Four Palo Alto friends start playing at thirteen, self-taught, in Torry Castellano's garage. The side project with matching Donna names ends up eating the main band.

years.cap: The four founding Donnas as teenagers
years.h: Four thirteen-year-olds form a band for a school show
years.p: [[The Donnas|d70416d3-c006-4a8b-aebd-91a4f198591f]] start in May 1993 in Palo Alto, playing Palo Alto High School's Day on the Green as Ragady Anne.
years.xp:
Brett Anderson, Allison Robertson, Maya Ford and Torry Castellano were all born in 1979 and taught themselves to play, practicing in Castellano's garage. Wikipedia lists the early names as Ragady Anne, then The Electrocutes, then The Donnas.

Anderson told the Grammy Awards site the group began as a side project and a joke, with the Electrocutes as the main band.

years.h: Matching stage names: Donna A, Donna R, Donna F, Donna C
years.p: Each member becomes a Donna by first initial, a Ramones-style gimmick that will stick for nearly a decade.

eras.title: Lookout! and the bubblegum punk sound
eras.text: Singles on Darin Raffaelli's Super*teem! and then Berkeley's Lookout! Records turn a high-school band into a touring act, with three albums in three years.

years.h: The Donnas: debut on Super*teem!
years.p: The self-titled first album comes out on Super*teem! Records and is later picked up by Lookout!.
years.xp: Producer Darin Raffaelli, who worked at a Mail Boxes Etc., recorded early singles there after hours, according to Anderson in the Grammy interview. She recalled the smell of the donut shop next door.

years.h: American Teenage Rock 'n' Roll Machine: ten songs, 24 minutes
years.p: Recorded at Trainwreck Studios in Oakland with the band and Romeo Voltage producing, it is their first Lookout! release.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists 32,000 US copies sold by 2005 per Nielsen SoundScan. Reviews ranged from Spin's 8/10 to Pitchfork's 6.8.

years.h: Five shows in Japan during senior year
years.p: The band flies to Japan for a week of gigs while still in high school.
years.xp: Anderson told Grammy.com she was sixteen at the time of the trip; Wikipedia places the tour in their senior year.

years.h: The Electrocutes appear in Drive Me Crazy
years.p: The band shows up on screen as The Electrocutes in the teen comedy and has songs on the Jawbreaker soundtrack.

years.h: Get Skintight: the sound goes big
years.p: Recorded at Toast in San Francisco with Jeff and Steve McDonald of [[Redd Kross|d3a4e499-19cf-4676-8aff-4a326b47cdb2]] producing, it adds a cover of Nikki Sixx's "Too Fast for Love".
years.xp: Fifteen tracks in 38 minutes. Wikipedia cites SoundScan for 58,000 US copies by 2005, and the reviews ran from Entertainment Weekly's B to The Village Voice's A-minus.

years.h: Detroit Rock City puts the Donnas on a big-screen Kiss film
years.p: The band appears in the Kiss teen movie, part of a year of movie tie-ins.

eras.title: Atlantic, TRL and Take It Off
eras.text: A major-label deal turns the Donnas into a hard-rock radio band with late-night slots and Lollapalooza.

years.h: The Donnas Turn 21: last Lookout! album
years.p: The fourth album closes their Lookout! run as the band turn twenty-one.

years.h: Atlantic Records signs the Donnas
years.p: Wikipedia dates the major-label deal to December 2001, ending the Lookout! years.

years.h: Spend the Night: major-label debut
years.p: Produced by Jason Carmer and Robert Shimp, it is their first Billboard 200 entry, peaking at 62 per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Lead single "Take It Off" reached No. 17 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart and the UK top 40. Wikipedia cites 450,000 US copies sold by 2005. A 2016 Cherry Red reissue added six bonus tracks.

years.h: TRL, SNL, Leno and Letterman in one year
years.p: The band plays Total Request Live, Saturday Night Live, The Tonight Show and Late Show with David Letterman.

years.h: Main stage at Lollapalooza
years.p: The Donnas play the main stage of the 2003 festival.

years.h: Gold Medal: Butch Walker at the board
years.p: Recorded in Hollywood in June and July 2004; the band drops its stage names and uses real names.
years.xp: Wikipedia says drummer Torry Castellano's wrist surgery pushed the songs to slower tempos, the DualDisc edition was recalled over a mastering error on the CD side, and the album peaked at 76 with 87,000 US copies by June 2007.

eras.title: Indie again, then a quiet end
eras.text: Leaving Atlantic, a shoulder injury and a drummer swap lead to a fade rather than a farewell.

years.h: Big Day Out in Australia
years.p: The band tours Australia with the festival and plays TV show Rove Live.

years.h: Amicable split with Atlantic
years.p: The band announces a mutual departure from the label.

years.h: Bitchin' on their own Purple Feather label
years.p: After the single "Don't Wait Up for Me" in March, the album comes out on Purple Feather Records.

years.h: Touring with Pat Benatar and Blondie
years.p: On the Call Me Invincible tour, Castellano is sidelined by shoulder tendonitis.

years.h: Torry Castellano retires from drumming
years.p: Amy Cesari of The Demonics replaces her.
years.xp: Castellano later studied at Stanford and Harvard Law School and works as an attorney, per Wikipedia.

years.h: A new song, "Tramp", and an unannounced end
years.p: The band premieres it at a private show while recording an eighth album, and Anderson later said they wrapped it up in 2012 without a farewell.
years.xp: Anderson told Grammy.com the group ended after seven albums with no farewell tour.

eras.title: Reissues and what came after
eras.text: The records stay in print while the members move to other lives.

years.h: Spend the Night reissued by Cherry Red
years.p: The reissue adds six bonus tracks.

years.h: Brett Anderson finishes a psychology degree
years.p: She began studies in 1997 and now works as a palliative-care social worker in Long Beach, per Grammy.com.

years.h: Early Singles 1995–1999 for Record Store Day
years.p: The compilation gathers the pre-Atlantic singles.
